title: The assigner numbered every committed entry it saw in insertion order, so a later inserter that committed while an earlier one was open could be numbered before it, contrary to the claimed commit order
resolution: Each entry stores its transaction id and the assigner numbers only entries below the snapshot xmin, in insertion order, without a writer lock (coordinator decision); gated PostgreSQL tests fail before the fix, and design decision 3 and the delta say so.

title: A browser stream started reading and delivering events before its first login check answered, and kept delivering while an expiry check was pending
resolution: Every login check runs inside the stream's read loop, which reads and delivers nothing until it answers, and a check that throws ends the stream; held-check tests fail before the fix.

title: A client that disconnected while the stream was opening left a registered stream and its keep-alive timer, and the sink kept writing to a destroyed response
resolution: The answer attaches no stream to a response already gone, and the sink refuses frames to and skips closing a gone response; a gated test fails before the fix.

title: The numbering loop awaited the LISTEN connection, which had no deadline and could not be closed while opening, so a stalled connection stopped the fallback poll and escaped shutdown
resolution: Each pass opens the connection beside its numbering, listen joins an opening attempt, the connection and each LISTEN get a 5 s deadline, and close ends one still opening; tests against a silent server fail before the fix.

title: The event stream route tests shared one log, hub, scheduler, and logger, and one test counted log records that later tests add, so another order failed
resolution: Each test builds and disposes its own stores, log, hub, and server; the old file fails under randomized order, and the new one passes alone per test and under eight seeds.

title: The spec, the wire contract, the design, and the migration promised insertion order for concurrent transactions, but a transaction's id is assigned at its first write, so the assigner orders by transaction age
resolution: The four places and the delta state the horizon rule in entry_id order without insertion order, and a PostgreSQL test pins an older transaction that wrote another table first being numbered first.

title: The item 14 line of wire contracts section 12 still named the board-changed events as item 14's, though item 15 emits them
resolution: The line names the event types and mapping of board-changed and card-changed, which item 15 emits.

title: The hub logged a stream overflow whenever the sink refused a frame, also for a client that was merely gone
resolution: The sink answers sent, full, or gone; only full logs the overflow and gone logs a neutral line; hub and HTTP tests fail before the fix.

title: An unnumbered row restored into a cluster whose transaction counter is below the row's transaction id would never be numbered or pruned
resolution: The numbering statement also numbers rows at or above its own snapshot xmax, which no transaction of the cluster can have (coordinator decision); a PostgreSQL test fails before the fix.

title: The numbering poll woke every stream each second even when it numbered nothing, so every idle stream ran a read each second
resolution: A numbering pass wakes the streams only when it numbered an entry; the numbered notification still always wakes them; keeper tests fail before the fix.

title: The test helper that waits for the numbering horizon polled in a tight loop without pause or overall bound
resolution: The helper polls every 20 ms and fails after 20 s, and a variant waits for one given transaction.

title: The records left task 6.2 unchecked, named a commit by its viewpoint instead of its hash, and had a double period
resolution: Tasks 6.2 and 6.3 are checked, the record names c1612367, and the double period is gone.

title: The LISTEN client set no TCP keep-alive and never probed its connection, so a half-open connection stayed counted as open
resolution: The client sets TCP keep-alive, and a listen on an open connection probes it with SELECT 1 under the deadline at most every 30 s; a frozen-proxy test fails before the fix.

title: PrincipalChange is defined in Access and in the execution log port, and nothing checked that the two shapes stay equal
resolution: A compile-time check in the adapter requires the stored forms of both types to be equal; drifts made in Access alone fail the build.

title: A role denial of the stream re-check after the bounds answered 401, and the project stream read its project before the re-check, so an unknown project answered 404 before 403
resolution: Both stream routes map role-required to 403, and the project stream's re-check checks the role before it reads the project; a route test whose server check passes and whose re-check denies fails before the fix.

title: The comment of BEFORE_ANY_EVENT still said item 14 would replace it, though this change did
resolution: The comment names the tests that wire no UI event log as the adapter's only users.

title: The Revision section still called 26bbb10f the merge base with origin/dev, which is f0ed0139 after the merge of dev
resolution: The section names 26bbb10f the development and checklist base and f0ed0139 the merge base since the merge of dev.

title: The self-check called migration 1792933700000 unused, though 20e's 1792933700000_scm-webhook-deliveries.sql is in the merged tree
resolution: The self-check keeps only 1792933600000 unused and names 20e's use of 1792933700000.

title: The evidence check attributed the generated block to verify-14-p3.log, though it records the merge verification
resolution: verify-14-merge.log, tree df394999 of eef15b3d, with 4485 tests, 4476 passed, none failed, and nine skipped, now writes the block; verify-14-p3.log is superseded.

title: The reconciliation named wire contracts sections 2 and 4 for #428's and #429's edits, which changed sections 4 and 5
resolution: The reconciliation names sections 4 and 5.
